utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, Madam Registrar. Could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-05-88-T, The Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic, et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you so much, ma'am. All the accused are present. Now, Prosecution it's Mr. McCloskey and Mr. Vanderpuye as yesterday. From the Defence teams I noted the absence of Ms. Tapuskovic, Mr. Nikolic, Mr. Bourgon, Mr. Petrusic and Mr. Haynes. I don't see the witness in the courtroom, does that mean there is a preliminary or something. Yes, Mr. Gosnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Just a brief scheduling note. One of the three witnesses who was scheduled to testify for this week after the current witness was denied a visa for entry into Holland.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It never rains but pours, you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: Which means we have one less witness than we expected this week and so I would simply wish to notify the Chamber that there is a possibility that we may be finishing earlier than expected on Friday. Particularly in light of some of the discussions we've had with the Defence about -- or the Prosecution about the length of cross-examination of the current witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right, okay. Thank you for keeping the Trial Chamber informed. If we can be of any assistance to you, please let us know. Now, the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, Professor. Welcome back. Mr. Lazarevic will finish his examination-in-chief. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning everybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Professor Bajagic.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I hope you had a good rest after yesterday. And I'm convinced that we will be able to finish your examination today. I am sure of my -- on my own behalf, I don't know about the others but we will do our best to finish your examination today.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday we left it off with the topic of the education centre in Mount Jahorina. I would like to pursue that same topic with a few questions to round the topic off. In your expert report, and I'm talking about paragraph 163 which is Exhibit 4D499, you have stated that there were actually two categories of military conscripts who had to be educated in the education centre on Mount Jahorina. The first category are recruits, young men who are being sent for compulsory military service who were supposed to do it in the Ministry of the Interior. That's the first category. And the second category, are deserters, i.e., military conscripts who were brought from Serbia and sent for education pursuant to documents that we saw yesterday. I would like to look at another document which is under tab 33 in your binder. This is Exhibit 4D352. While we are waiting for this to appear in e-court, I'm going to say that this is information sent by the assistant commander Dusko Jevic. The date is 13 July 1995, and the information was sent to the Ministry of the Interior to the special police brigade at the Jahorina training camp. This is actually a daily report as we have said. What I would like to look at with regard to this document is the first paragraph thereof, the last sentence. It says according to the list, 201 conscripts and 35 recruits doing their military service, so conscripts is here represented by what abbreviation?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: VO.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: 35 recruits doing their military service in the MUP are currently staying at the Jahorina mission and training centre. Is that exactly what you're talking about in your paragraph 163? Are these the two categories that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, these are the two categories of persons who were sent to the Jahorina training camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well, and now could you please look at paragraph 165 of your expert report, you say in it that the deserters in the Jahorina training camp had nothing but basic military training. The training that they had to undergo, did it have anything to do with the education of MUP members, especially members of the special police?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my paragraph 165, I presented this fact and say that military conscript training had absolutely nothing whatsoever to do with what was supposed to be education for any kind of engagement in the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Especially it didn't have anything to do with the education of future members of any special police unit because we know from various experiences across the world that it takes a lot of time to train somebody to become a member of a special police unit. In this case, a special police brigade. It takes anything between one year and three years for such education.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And just one more question, a rather general one with regard to this topic. We have already heard many times that when it comes to this mixed unit that was placed under the command of Mr. Borovcanin encompassed the second detachment of the special police Sekovic, the first company of the Zvornik special units and a company of military conscripts who had been in training at the Jahorina camp. Could you please tell us what your conclusion was in your expert report with this regard? Was this unit a unit with homogeneous nature?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In any case, this unit that Mr. Borovcanin received pursuant to an order was not [Realtime transcript read in error "was"] homogeneous because there were three different groups or members in that unit. It was an ad hoc unit. One group were members of the special police brigade, another group were members of the PJP, and the third part were those who had arrived from the training camp who had never been in any other education and they were only informed with the basic rules of service at Jahorina training camp. This did not last more than 15 or 20 days and they were not prepared to act at a level that a homogenous unit should have and they were not allowed to participate in any kind of engagement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just for the record, I would like to say that when we are talking about units that --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please slow down especially when quoting numbers. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I would now like to -- yes. The exhibit that I mentioned is 4D337. This is order 64/95, but I did not think it necessary to show it again because we have had several occasions to look at that particular document that I was referring to in this particular question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I apologise for intervention to my colleague, but I notice in page 5, it appears to be line 5 that the witness's answer doesn't appear to reflect what he said and it specifically refers to homogenous unit at that line, homogenous unit should have and they were not allowed to participate in any kind of activity, I don't believe that is what the witness actually testified to, and so I wonder if my colleague could clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, my colleague is right. I am grateful. I believe that we all need to have a clear record on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You see, Mr. Bajagic, in the transcript we have it that you were talking about the unit composed of deserters and it says here in the transcript that they were not allowed to participate in any form of activity but I believe that you said that they were not adequately or sufficiently trained do that?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that they were not adequately and sufficiently trained, I didn't say that they were not allowed to be engaged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I appreciate that. But it's still unclear as to what activity the witness is talking about. I know that wasn't in the original answer but I would also ask if my colleague would clarify that as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe it's clear now. It's just -- activities were not mentioned at all in the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: They were not mentioned but this is precisely what Mr. Vanderpuye is asking. Perhaps the witness can state exactly what kind of activity/activities we were talking about or we could be talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Professor, I'll try and clarify this matter. When we are talking about activities of this mixed unit, combat activities, were they adequately trained to participate in such activities?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The part of the unit or members of that unit who had arrived from the Jahorina training centre on mount Jahorina were not adequately trained. They were deserters, they were not adequately trained in order to be able to respond to any such task. That would be my answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Is my colleague satisfied with the answer or do I need further clarifications.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: No, it's fine. If there's any cross, I'll undertake it. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Professor Bajagic, my next topic, since I believe that we have exhausted the training centre on Jahorina is the training centre of the MUP of the Republika Srpska in the period of immediate threat of war or the conditions of war. I would like to go to that rather first. I would like to say that we are talking about paragraphs between 169 and 195 of your expert report. In this regard, I would like you to look at the document under tab 15. It is 4D413. I would like to look at a few articles of the law on the implementation of the Law on the Interior during an immediate threat of war or war. Let's first look at Article 2. Looking at this article, could you tell me whether pursuant to Article 2 when war is proclaimed or an imminent threat of war, the Law on the Interior continues to be applied unless differently specified by another law.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The provisions of other laws are applied unless this law strictly specifies something else. The answer is yes. The provisions of the Law on the Interior are still applied.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. With this regard, in order to be as expeditious as possible, I would like to look at Article 12 of the same law. Article 12 defines and says that in addition to the special units of the police, the Minister of the Interior can also establish other special police units who will be engaged in combat. Please, could you tell us pursuant to this law, these are the only two categories of police units that appear in this law?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Special police units and specialised police units, that's what is provided for by the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I will not dwell upon this point. I would like to move on to the third chapter of your report, which is command and control in the MUP of Republika Srpska. Again to be expeditious, I'd like to say that before this Trial Chamber we have heard a lot about the terms of command and control. I'll skip the terminology and the determinants of the terms control command and management and I will move on to the control and command in the police. I would just like to point your attention to paragraphs between 196 and 205 of your expert report which are on pages 54 to 57, or rather 53 to 56 in e-court. And I would also like to say that in your expert report, you speak about the command and control in police in general terms in paragraphs 206 and 226, I will not further analyse these paragraphs in this examination-in-chief, I would just like to analyse paragraph 228. Do you have that in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In your paragraph 228 you -- I apologise, you have analysed the functions of command and control in the police and you mention nine subfunctions. Just for the record could you please quote your nine functions that you mention in this paragraph and that fall under command and control?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Command and control implicate tasks and duties that supervising officers and chiefs perform in the course of their work. These functions are as follows: Under 1 monitoring and assessment. Number 2, decision-making. Number 3, planning. 4, organising. 5, order issuing. 6, coordination. 7, controlling. 8, affirmation and representation. And finally number 9, analysis and evaluation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. You are now talking about control?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely so. I specified that this is control rather than command. So this is control.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise, there seems to be -- it is okay. I'm just trying to follow the record in order to make it absolutely clear to anybody who may be reading it in the future. The next topic that you dealt with in your expert report is the control of the police when performing special security tasks. I'm not going to ask you anything about that. I would just like to address everybody's attention to paragraphs 266 to 284 in your expert report.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Paragraphs 268 to paragraph 284.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I would like to look at paragraph 286 of your expert report dealing with the control in the MUP of Republika Srpska at the level of the police forces staff. In paragraph 286, you define the police force staff. Could you please tell us how you define it in your own words?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my paragraph 286, I say that the police force staff as an organ of control and command in organ of police units is defined as a provisional body which is activated when police units are engaged more extensively in combat actions and in discharging more complex police duties in special security circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I would now like us to look at a document which is in your binder under tab 36, and in e-court it is Exhibit 4D179. This is an order, the date is 15 May 1992. On page 2 we can see that it was signed by the Minister of the Interior of the then Serbian republic of Republika Srpska Mr. Mico Stanisic. Do you have the document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I would like us to look at bullet point 9 in this document. Could you please read that paragraph for us, and also who are the members of the staff envisaged by this order?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This order speaks about the establishment of the staff, amongst other things. And it says that in order to command and control the overall forces of ministry staff shall be established comprising; Minister of the Interior, as its commander; under secretary for public security, deputy commander; under secretary for national security, member. Assistant ministers for crime, police, communications, and crypto protection, materiel and finance. These assistants are members. Commander of the police detachment, member; deputy commander of the police detachment, member; chiefs of security service centres, members, and also chef de cabinet of the minister as the secretary. This would be the full composition of the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Therefore this is the composition of the police force staff?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The next document I would like us to analyse is your tab 37. It is Exhibit 4D189. The date is the 25th of August 1992 sent to the chief of the public security station in Prijedor. The title is "Instruction on the Training and use of Public Security Units in Banja Luka or the Banja Luka CSB." I'd like us to look at page 3 of the document, items 3.1 and 3.2 which are on page 4 in your document.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It is page 7 in the English e-court version. As for the use of wartime units, well, that was the title that preceded these points. Can you please comment 3.1 and 3.2?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This concerns the use of wartime units. Under 3.1 it says that the Banja Luka CSB shall govern the use of war units within the Banja Luka CSB and the SJB staff shall govern the use of SJB units. That was 3.1. Under 3.2, it says that the commander, his deputy or chief, or the Chief of Staff shall order -- I'll repeat. 3.2: The commander, his deputy or chief or the Chief of Staff shall order the use of CSB units in collaboration with the armed forces of the Serbian republic. The Ministry of the Interior of the Serbian republic shall be informed of this as a matter of urgency. This means the very top of the ministry [Realtime transcript read in error "military"] will be notified.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. We have a designation of who has the commanding authority over the use of wartime units; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: A correction for the transcript. It's on page 11, line 25 said ministry will be notified. Line 23, I apologise. Says at the very top the ministry will be notified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lazarevic. All right, okay, thank you. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Next is paragraph 289 in your expert report. In it you state that given the centralised model of organisation of the RS MUP there was a relation of hierarchy between the MUP police force staff of the RS and the CJB staffs. Is it the same type of hierarchy which exists, as you've already explained on your charts, between the MUP at headquarters and the centres for public security?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I fail to understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I'll reformulate. I presume you have paragraph 289 of your report in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Therein you state -- well, I wanted to draw a parallel between the hierarchy concluding the MUP at headquarters and CSBs, and to see whether the same kind of hierarchy exists between the RS MUP staff in relation to the various CJB staffs.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the hierarchy is the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let us move on to the next topic, and that is the regulations regulating the use of MUP units in wartime activities. We've had occasion to see the law from 1994 which is the law on the implementation of the Law on Internal Affairs. It is your tab 15. Let us have a look at item 3.2, that is to say, Article 13, paragraph 2. It is page 5 in e-court. In the English page 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It's 4D413. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In item 2 of Article 13 it says that the Ministry of the Interior controls police units through the police force staffs at the headquarters; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And this ties in with the units of the police special police units and specialized police units that we discussed?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And this only refers to those units which were not resubordinated in keeping with this regulation to the military unit within whose area of responsibility they were engaged in combat?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this refers to the units of the police which acted independently in pursuing their tasks and duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. The next document I'd like to have a look at is your tab 38. In e-court it is 4D138. The date on the document is first the 29th of October 1994 and then the 31st of October 1994. MUP of the RS Sarajevo. Can you tell me who is on the distribution list?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document, order was sent to all administrations of the state security department and the public security department to all public security centres, and to all state security department centres, to all public security stations, and to the school of the interior in Banja Luka. That is to say, to everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I wanted to go briefly through the document. Sorry to interrupt. Let us look at the preamble. What does it say?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says that this is a very urgent document. Do you mean that?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No, go on.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it says in accordance with an order issued by the minister, and the order of the president of the republic declaring a state of war. It means that this order is created on the basis of the previous two orders specified.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And we see that it has to do with the proclamation of a state of war in at least one part of the republic which is the AOR of the 2nd Corps. Can you please look at item 1 of the order?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to item 1 of the order, all public and state security centres shall form joint staffs which will control all police forces in their respective areas and will be subordinated to the police forces command staff of the MUP of Republika Srpska. That is to say, the headquarters at the seat of the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: According to the second paragraph of item 1, who is included in such staffs?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The staffs comprise the following: Chief of the CJB as the head of staff, then deputy chief of the CJB as deputy head of staff, chief of the state security department centre as member. Next is chief of the police department or sector as member. And then we have the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but that is because it spills over to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Commander of the PJP as member. Then chief of the crime police sector as member. And chief of the communications department as member.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And this document sets out the composition of such staffs?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the composition of such a staff at the level of a public security centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In relation to this document, let us look at its last paragraph. Can you tell us what it prescribes?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It defines that any further operational or operative plan of all staffs will be drafted by the Chief of Staff of the MUP of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, the Chief of Staff of the police forces of the RS is assigned a function here specifying his authority in the order.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: As regards the staffs, let us look at the next document which is tab 39 in your binder. It is Exhibit 4D280. It is a dispatch, number K/5-1-248/95 dated 1 June 1995.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I believe you have the document in front of you.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us see the distribution list.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document was sent to the heads of the two departments, that is to say, the state security and public security department, to the staff of the police forces command in Bijeljina, to the special police brigade at Jahorina, to the SJB at Pale, and then we have three police stations and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps we can stop here. Let's look at who sent this dispatch.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says that it was sent by minister Zivko Rakic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In the first paragraph it says that the minister is forming a staff to command and control the police forces in Pale comprising the following people, among other names we can see Mr. Borovcanin's name on the list. I'm interested in particular in the last sentence of the dispatch. Can you tell us what was the reason to establish this staff?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As we can see from the last sentence, this staff was formed in view of the newly created complex security situation in the wider location of Pale municipality as a consequence of the NATO bombardment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. We are done with this document. Let us look next at your tab 42. In e-court it is Exhibit 4D139. Do you have the document before you?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: On the first page of the document the date is 17 June 1995. Sent by head of office Nenad Radovic. It says: "Please find enclosed the conclusions from the Minister of the Interior specialist staff meeting held on 16 June 1995 in Pale. You must comply with them and inform the office of the minister about their implementation." I'd like us to look at the next page. The date there is the 16th of June. We can see the conclusions from the specialist staff meeting referred to on page 1. Let's look at item 1, subitem (4).

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: What is this about? What conclusion was reached at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The conclusion was that staff should be established to control the police forces. Its seat would be in the Tron facility in Pale.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well, let's move on to the following document which is under tab 40 in your binder. This is Exhibit 4D140 dispatch number K/5 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: K/P307/95 dated 19 June 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It is obvious that this document is connected with the previous one. Could you please tell us in the first paragraph which starts with "we wish to inform you that ..." What is this about?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says that a staff has been formed to command police forces in the zone in which a state of war has been declared and a list is given of its composition.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are seven names here, am I supposed to read them? I don't think this would be necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Of course not, everybody can see it. But after the names it says and it lists the duties of the Sarajevo CJB and the Srbinje [Realtime transcript read in error "Serbia"] CJB have in keeping with the dispatch, what would these be, also these include the special brigade?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Sarajevo and Srbinje [Realtime transcript read in error "Serbia"] CJB's have a duty to inform the CJBs in their areas about the existence of that staff, i.e., that the staff has been established. And also the command of the special police brigade is also duty-bound to inform all special police detachments.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well, we will continue and pursue this topic but I need to make a correction in the transcript, which is on page 17, line 22, it says here Serbia and we were talking about Srbinje; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let's look at the penultimate paragraph of this dispatch which says the staff's headquarters are in the Tron facility in Pale, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This confirms that the conclusion reached at the ministry meeting, i.e., one of the orders contained therein.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: When we are talking about this staff headquartered in Tron this would be the same staff that effectively was in command of the police forces or in control of the police forces in June 1995 as it is referred to in paragraph 295 of your expert report. This would be the same staff?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was no other staff established. It's the one and the same staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In order to simplify things for the Trial Chamber when it comes to the staff, I would like us to look at the thing that can be found under tab 72 in your binder, which is the schematic that can be found in Exhibit 4D459. Do you have the schematic in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please explain the schematic for us. Here we have two types of lines. One is the lines of command or control responsibility which is represented by a full line and the second schematic is represented by a dotted line which depicts the line of cooperation or influence. Wouldn't that be correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You are absolutely right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please provide some explanation. In the upper part of this schematic there's the Supreme Command from which an arrow leads to the line of command or control responsibility towards the minister.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the upper part we have an elliptic circle depicting the words Supreme Command and a line leading to the Minister of the Interior. We also have a dotted line leading in the opposite direction which shows the position of the Minister of the Interior in the Supreme Command as a member of the Supreme Command. Further on we follow the line of command under the minister, there is the staff of the police forces and again it says here that the minister is also the commander and this staff also has its chief and its members. We already spoke about that either yesterday or the day before. We mentioned the exact composition of that staff. And below that is special police brigade staff controls the units of the Ministry of the Interior as one of the two components of the armed forces, we are talking about the bolded square or rectangular. Further on we have two lines leading towards the special police brigade in the left lower corner and right of that and below the units of the Minister of the Internal Affairs, we also have separate police units or PJPs. Between the special police brigade and the separate police units or PJPs, there is a dotted line with arrows on both ends of that line, which implies that these two types of police units do engage in certain form of cooperation but there is no other hierarchical or command or subordination relationship between the two. In other words, they are at an equal footing because they stand on the same line, so to speak.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well then. Could you please explain the right part of this schematic starting with the police forces staff. Could you please explain the command line towards the public security centre?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a full line between the minister and the public security sector and from there to the police administration which is only natural given the organisational structure of the ministry. From the police forces staff, there is a line on the right-hand side leading to the public security centres. You see that it says the commander of PJP which is only natural because the police forces staff should have a control line leading to the commander of the PJP and the chief of the public security centre and somewhat further to the left, we also have a situation that from the public security sector there is a line with very short arrows leading to the administration of the centre of the public security centres because they are part of the sector of public security, and we also have a very short dotted line from the police administration towards public security centres and this represents the model of cooperation and influence which is normal in planning and some other activities that are undertaken by the two, which means that the administration of the police as a professional organ within the security sector has a capacity to be able to realise a form of cooperation in professional terms and they have influence on the level that implies the public security centres and this is what this schematic represents.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Off mic, the counsel is off mic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that we will no longer need this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: According to this schematic, the special police brigade is directly subordinate to the units of the Ministry of Internal Affairs but theoretically speaking but special police brigade is not a subordinate organ of the unit of the MUP. Rather, it is directly subordinate to the ministry or minister?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, if maybe we can -- maybe we can explain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I understand. I would understand the witness wanted to emphasize the units of the ministry as one of the component of armed forces. But if you look at the PJP in this schematic, while it is directly subordinated to CJB or public security centre, it is also directly subordinated to the minister or the units of The Ministry of Internal Affairs. If you could clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'll do my best.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have already had an opportunity to talk about the law on the application of the Law on the Interior or the Law on Internal Affairs, and we have already emphasized that the minister through the staff controls the police units that are engaged in combat. Wouldn't that be correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Now, if we look at the command line here in the schematic leading from the minister, it leads across the police forces staff to the unions of the Ministry of the Internal Affairs?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And as far as I can understand, you have only separated the units of the Ministry of the Internal Affairs into special police brigade of the police and separate police units or PJPs in keeping with the law on the application of the Law on Internal Affairs during an imminent threat of war or war?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In other words, the minister also controls the special and separate police units through the police forces staff?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The minister controls all police units through the police forces staff according to this law.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Irrespective of the nature of the police units, be it the special police brigade which is under the direct command of the minister or separate police units?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's why the police forces staff has been established in the first place.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And at the same time the minister is also the commander of the police forces staff; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is clear. Here below the minister it says commander, in brackets, minister and I believe it is self-explanatory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If I can be more clear. So the thing is that the minister can command and control PJP either directly or through CJB, that's what the witness emphasized. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's move on to the next document which is under tab 41 in your binder, and the exhibit number in e-court is 4D295. This is a decision by the president of Republika Srpska on the proclamation of the state of war in the zone of responsibility of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps dated 17 June 1995. What I would like us to look at in particular is item 3 of this decision.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: What armed forces are referred to herein? In what zone, rather.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is referring to the zone of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps. This decision on declaring a state of war provides that all armed forces are duty-bound to take on necessary measures to achieve the defined aims and in light of the date which is 17 June 1995, we know what had been provided by the law dating from autumn 1994. We know what is implied by armed forces. Armed forces imply two components, those are the Army of Republika Srpska is the first component of the armed forces, and units of the Ministry of the Interior as the second components of the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now, I would like to move on to the next document in your binder. It is number 44 and in e-court it is 4D294. This is a dispatch from the command of the Herzegovina Corps conveying the decision of the president of Republika Srpska on the proclamation of a state of war in the municipalities of [indiscernible], Srbinje, Cajnice, Ruda, Visegrad, Gorazde and Rogatica. This dispatch bears the date of the 17 of June 1995 and now let's look at page 2 under bullet point 1.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Where were these municipalities, in the zone of what corps?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The municipalities listed in this document are in the zone of the Drina Corps and parts of the zone of the Herzegovina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: With this regard, I would like us to look at the following document which is number 45 in your binder, and in the e-court system it is Exhibit number 4D340. This is a decision on declaring a state of war in the municipalities of Srebrenica and Skelani. The date is 14 July 1995, and let's just look at the first bullet point of this decision.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see this. According to this decision, a state of war is proclaimed in the territory of the municipalities of Srebrenica-Skelani.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Is this document in relation with the previous one on declaring a state of war in the municipalities falling in the AOR of the Drina and Herzegovina Corps?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is another decision on the declaration of a state of war in one part of the RS territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: To conclude with this set of documents, the next one I'd like us to look at is tab 46 in your binder. In e-court it is 4D351. The date is the 28th of July 1995. Decision on the proclamation of a state of war in the territory of the whole of Republika Srpska declared by president of the republic Karadzic. Is this in relation with the previous two documents?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. However, for the first time in this decision, a state of war is being declared in the territory of the whole of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I have a few documents left that have to do with the declaration of a state of war. This is tab 74 in your binder, whereas in e-court it is 4D218.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It is a decision on the establishment of war presidencies in the municipalities during a state of war. Let's look at item 1.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Have a look at item 4 as well whereby there is some mention of cooperation on the part of the war presidencies.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it says that during the state of war --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, item 1.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- that war presidencies will be established in the municipalities of the Serbian city of Sarajevo. In item 4 certain obligations of such presidencies are mentioned entailing standing and direct cooperation with unit commands in the area of the municipalities with a view to coordinating and informing all state institutions in the territory of the given municipality in matters important for defence and life of the population.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did war presidencies have any command competencies over say MUP units?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Although they were called war presidencies, these were civilian organs. They had no authority over any structures of the MUP or the army of the RS.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's go to tab 75 next. In e-court it is 4D354. It is a dispatch from the office of the Minister of the Interior of the RS dated the 2nd of August 1995. It was sent to all RJBs, CJBs, and SJBs. Do you have the document?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the part of the document which says: "Pursuant to these guidelines ..." What does this document refer to when mentioning such guidelines?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is in direct relation with my previous statement. From the level of the ministry, this dispatch is being sent to those mentioned on the distribution list stating that municipal war presidencies cannot issue any orders to centres and stations of public security, since those are MUP units and such are part of the Armed Forces of Republika Srpska. Those forces are controlled by the minister, as stated herein. It is also stressed by this dispatch that the minister executes the orders of the president of the republic who is the Supreme Commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us move to the next document next. It is your tab 47. In e-court 4D247. It is an order signed for the minister Zivko Rakic who was the then internal minister of the RS. The date is the 30th of March 1995. Let's have a look at the order. It talks about the first Jahorina special police detachment to be sent in combat against sabotage and terrorist groups in the area of Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I'm interested in the second paragraph. It says that: "The police forces staff of the Zvornik CJB is to control all the MUP forces in executing a combat task along the axis Vlasenici-Zvornik."

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This document entitles the CJB centre with controlling all MUP forces along that axis?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In relation to that, let's have a look at another document which is tab 48.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I apologise again for the intervention but it appears to me that the record is unclear that the witness's conclusion that it entitles the police forces staff of the Zvornik CJB to control all the MUP forces when that axis should be tied to the particular order and the particular date. That is the assignment that is specified in the order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Lazarevic would you look into that, please. I think Mr. Vanderpuye is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but the document is self-explanatory. It says I think what are the capacity of the MUP staff from CJB Zvornik in this respect in this very particular operation from March 1995. I'm not suggesting anything other than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, no, I think --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That's fine, Mr. Lazarevic. I just want the record to be clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's fine. Let's proceed then, please, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you have the document before you? It should be your tab 48.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It is 4D387. A dispatch sent from the CJB Zvornik sent by head of centre Dragomir Vasic on the 21st of March 1995. As stipulated therein, it says that the subject is a report from the meeting of the centre police forces staff. I'm interested in the first paragraph. It says: "Acting on your order, on the 21st of March 1995, a meeting of the police forces staff of the Zvornik public security centre was held ... " and then there is an analysis provided. We can conclude from the document that on the 21st of March 1995, there had already been a police forces staff at the Zvornik public security centre in existence?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is obvious.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the next document. It is your tab 49. The Exhibit number is 4D333. Do you have it in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Briefly then it is a dispatch sent on the 9th of July 1995 sent from the public security centre in Zvornik. What was the function or the capacity of Dragomir Vasic given the fact that he signed the document?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Dragomir Vasic signed this as the staff commander of the police forces of the public security centre in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let's look at the next document. It is your tab 50. The date is the 10th of July 1995. Again we see that it was signed for staff commander Dragomir Vasic but it was signed by someone else.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Is this in relation to ...

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we can see that the first one was the 9th of July, the second was 10th of July. We see that the staff was in operation and the documents were signed by Dragomir Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the next document. It is your tab 51, 4D339. Another dispatch of the 12th of July 1995 sent from Zvornik and let's look again at the signature block. Who signed the document and in what capacity?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says Dragomir Vasic, he signed it as the staff commander of the police forces of the public security centre in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: To round off the topic, we'll use the next document, which is tab 52. In e-court it is 4D --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: P66.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The date is 1 August 1995. It is sent by Dragomir Vasic. Let's focus on the first paragraph which reads: "Pursuant to your dispatch, we held a meeting of the war staff of the centre that has been in operation as of the date of your order of the 21st of March 1995." Based on the documents we just saw, it is obvious that the war staff at the centre existed at that time. According to the documents we saw, it began functioning at the latest on the 21st of March 1995, and it was also operational in the month of August of 1995?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. These are the facts. It says here the 21st of March. It means that it was the latest day as of which it started operating and it lasted at least until August as referred to in the documents. That is my conclusion, that the staff was in operation at least during that period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In order to deal with all the issues that need to be clarified thoroughly, I ask you this. This staff controlled all MUP units that were in the territory of Zvornik municipality save for the police units that were sent to various AORs and were under the command of the various corps?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the police forces staff of the centre in Zvornik was the controlling body of all police units that were in the territory of the centre of Zvornik. All police units that were in the area were under the command of that staff except of course for the units which were made part of the army of the RS, which were of a different nature.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. To round off the topic of staffs, let's look at the next document, which is your tab 53. In e-court it is 4D245. A dispatch sent from the command of the staff of police forces. The date is the 25th of March 1995. Do you have it before you?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: According to this document, can we conclude that there were certain problems with the procedure of police forces being engaged in combat, as specified herein, it says that certain personnel in managerial positions tried to bypass the prescribed procedure requesting the use of police forces?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Judging by this document, I conclude that certain people tried to bypass the prescribed procedure requesting and arranging for the police forces in combat operations. In the latter part of the dispatch we can see that minister Zivko Rakic is requesting that all engagement of MUP forces in combat be arranged only through the main command of the police forces of the MUP as the only body competent and responsible for such matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I think I'll be able to finish within 20 to 25 minutes. This was a very serious topic and I really needed to cover it deeply.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, we wouldn't restrain you in any way, Mr. Lazarevic. We'll have a 25-minute break starting from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bajagic, I will do my utmost to move speedily. In order to clarify a couple of things from your testimony which -- concerning some things which took place this morning, let's go back to your tab 47. It is 4D00247. Let us look at the distribution list of this order.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This order was sent to the command of the special police brigade to the command of the first detachment of the special police at Jahorina and to the centre for training of police dogs and horses.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And it transpires from this order as it does from the schematic that we have already analysed, let's not go back to it, that there is the first special police detachment as seated on Jahorina, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And this first detachment has nothing whatsoever to do with the centre for education on Jahorina?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. It has nothing whatsoever to do -- the first detachment has nothing whatsoever to do with it. It's just one of the nine detachments of the special police brigade which is located on Jahorina just like the centre was located on Jahorina, but these are two different things.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In other words, this is a geographical coincidence?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the same area.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well, I believe and I hope that this is now clear, and now I would like to move on to the next chapter in your expert report, which is reporting in the Ministry of the Interior, and I would like us to look at a document that is under tab 57 in your -- 54 in your binder.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This is 4D193 in e-court. This is an instruction on urgent ongoing and statistical reporting. This is a rather comprehensive document. My question to you is this: The basic document that regulates the issue of reporting within the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the basic document in the form of an instruction about all forms of reporting within the Republika Srpska MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In order to speed things along, I would like us to look at your expert report, paragraph 304 in your expert report. The Exhibit number is 4D499. In keeping with this instruction that we have just seen in e-court, could you please tell us firstly in paragraph 304 you have explained the notion of urgent reporting. What are the two types of urgent reporting within the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Among the four main aspects of reporting in the Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska, one of them is urgent reporting which can be carried out in two ways. The first one would be written reporting by way of documents also known as dispatches, and secondly, orally by way of means of communications, mostly telephone.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well, let's move on to paragraph 308 on the following page of your expert report. Here you deal with current and ongoing or occasional reporting. Could you please tell us in keeping with the book of rules that we have just had an opportunity to look at, what would be the definition of current reporting as opposed to occasional reporting?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are two aspects of reporting within the MUP. The first one is current reporting which implies written information or sending of written information about one or several security events and measures that were undertaken with respect to any of these events. On the other hand, the written information can be collective analysis or overviews, as well as all forms of urgent reporting. On the other hand, occasional reporting is carried out in the form of various types of analyses and reports about certain incidents or events or a single event, phenomenon or integral information submitted by the regional organs of the interior and I'm referring here to public security centres and stations. As well as some other information that concern the activities of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Now let's move on to paragraph 310 of your expert report which is statistical reporting. And just briefly in keeping with this instruction, what are the forms or aspects of statistical reporting and how is statistical reporting carried out?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Statistical report is carried out by means of sending various reports on previously designed statistical forms. There are several forms of statistical reporting. Under 1 it would be regular reporting, under number 2 it would be monthly, number 3 would be quarterly, number 4 would be half yearly, and number 5 would be annual statistical reporting.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And now I would like to ask you this: Based on the documents that you perused and analysed would you say that there were some problems with the application of this instruction when it comes to the reporting within the MUP of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the last paragraphs of this chapter of my expert report I have mentioned some examples of operation from the established procedure which is defined by the instruction on reporting and informing. I'm talking about several or just a few situations that I have singled out based on the documents that I had an occasion to use when drafting my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. These are the two or three documents that I would like us now to see. First of all, let's look at tab 55 in your binder. In e-court this is 4D204. This is a dispatch by the assistant minister Tomislav Kovac dated 24 July 1993 sent to all CSB chiefs and to all SJB chiefs. I would like to draw your attention to the first paragraph starting with the words "public security stations". Could you please read the sentence starting with the words "public security stations do not submit their reports in time or not at all and they in turn do not report to the MUP headquarters"?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Does this refer to the reporting procedure envisaged by the instruction from the public security stations to the security services centres and then to the MUP headquarters?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is how things should have been in keeping with the instruction. However, some omissions in the procedure have been noticed and addressed here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And now let's look at the second paragraph, referring to an order that is being issued to the chiefs mentioned in the dispatch. It says here that public security stations are hereby ordered that as of 1st of August 1993, and can you please look at the rest of the sentence, "... daily informed the authorised CSBs about security events in their areas, and the centres will then process information received from the stations in the form of a 'daily bulletins' and deliver them by dispatch to the MUP by no later than 2400 hours of the day in question." Is this what you've just spoken about in regard to the procedure?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is just another reinforcement of the order issued to the public security stations and security services centres asking them to adhere to the procedure on future reporting starting with the 1st of August 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well then. Let's look at the penultimate paragraph of the dispatch.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here that the SJBs and centres are still obliged to inform the MUP about certain important occurrences as soon as they learn about such occurrences.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And now, the last paragraph of this dispatch. According to this dispatch, who will be responsible for the execution of this assignment?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The SJB chiefs and the CSB chiefs are directly responsible for the execution of this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The next document that I would like us to look at should be under tab 56 in your binder. These are the provisions of the instruction on all kinds of reporting and other documents. The date is 19 April 1995, and let's not go and repeat the addressees. Just below that, there's something that I would like to look at. The sentence starts with the words: "We are drawing your attention once again ..." I apologise, this is Exhibit 4D256.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It says here reiterate the need to strictly observing reporting regulations. Would this confirm what you've already spoken about?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this confirms that there have been occurrences when instructions were not observed, and attention is once again drawn to the need to obey the procedure when it comes to all sorts of reporting, i.e., the instruction that we just looked at.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And now, let's look at the last document that I've prepared for the examination-in-chief with regard to the topic of informing and reporting in the MUP. It's under tab 57 in your binder, and this is Exhibit 4D273 in the e-court system.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This is another dispatch by minister Zivko Rakic bearing the date 25 -- 20 of September 1995. It is clear who the addressees are. Let's look at the first paragraph for the time being, the starting words are: "We hereby inform you of the need for consistent implementation of the instruction on urgent, current, occasional and statistical reporting." Does this point to the fact?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does. This is already the third situation that I became aware of. Dispatches sent to reiterate the need to strictly observe the instruction.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the last paragraph of this dispatch, what does it say?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here that the dispatch is to be considered an amendment to the previously mentioned instruction and it also says here that a failure to abide by all the provisions of that instruction shall constitute a violation of duty within the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well then. Let's on move on to the next -- actually the last part of your expert report dealing with ranks and functional insignia in the MUP of Republika Srpska, my general first question is this: When it comes to ranks and functional insignia in the MUP can they be compared with the military ranks and functional insignia? I apologise. There are no functional insignia in the military at all so just dealing with ranks.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to what I could conclude drafting my report and otherwise ranks and functional insignia in the Ministry of the Interior including the Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska differ from the ranks in the Armed Forces, i.e., the military.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let's look at your tab 58 which is Exhibit 4D103. This is an order on uniform functions and insignia in the police. Number is 404/76-92 dated 21 October 1992. And obviously this provides for the wearing of uniforms and functional insignia in the MUP. Let's immediately go to page 20 in B/C/S or page 10 in the English version of this document. You have them on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Are these the functional insignia worn by the police?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These are insignia of positions or functional insignia in the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And now can we look at Article 13 of this decree. In e-court this is on pages 9 and 10 in B/C/S and on pages 5 and 6 in English. As may be seen in the title, the chapter deals with functions and functional insignia. I'm not going to go into the details of all of these functions. I would just like to ask you this: According to this decree, there are no ranks of captain major, captain or lieutenant in the police?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are right. Functional insignia do not imply the use of those particular terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In order to explain the genesis of functional relationships and ranks, I would like us to look at the following document which concerns this particular matter. This is the law on the promulgation of the law on amendments to the Law of Interior dated 31st of December 1994. In your case this is tab 59. On page 2 we can see Article 1178 [as interpreted]. This is on page 2 of the B/C/S version and in English it is on page 3. What can you tell us about that?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, could you please repeat the number of this article?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: 1178 [as interpreted]. This is Exhibit number 208 in e-court, page 2 in B/C/S, page 3 in English.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Article 117A speaks about the introduction of ranks in the ministry for authorised officials, that is to say, for several categories of authorised officials.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us move on to the next tab in your binder. It is number 60. It is 4D279. While we are waiting for the English version, tell us this, please, this regulation, in its lower right-hand corner includes corrections to the law on the amendments to the Law on Internal Affairs, isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were several corrections and amendments to the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The date is the 28th of May 1995?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The next document I'd like us to look at is your tab 61. It is 4D259. Decision on the establishment of ranks and functions and promotion to police ranks of authorised officials of the MUP. The number is 01-713/95 dated the 20th of April 1995. Let's have a look at Article 25. It is the last article. In its final provisions it says that the Minister of the Interior within 30 days following the decision will issue the table of ranks for authorised officials?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Therefore the deadline was set at 30 days?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, 30 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Were there any problems in the field when implementing this task of conferring the ranks?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I presume there was a problem. All of the events in the first and the second half of 1995 must have slowed down the implementation of all administrative acts put in force by the ministry as regards such administrative nature tasks which had to be implemented in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us move to the next document. It is tab 62. Exhibit 4D243. It is a dispatch of minister Zivko Rakic. The date is 14 of March 1995. In item 1 it says that on the 18th of March 1995 there will be a session of the expanded collegium of the MUP. Let us look at the agenda. It's item 3.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: What is it about?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Among other items on the agenda of the meeting of the expanded collegium of the ministry, the item 3 should have been dedicated to information on the draft decision on the establishment of ranks in the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the next document. It is 63 in your binder. Exhibit 4D257. It is another dispatch by minister Zivko Rakic. The date is the 19th of April 1995.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The beginning of the dispatch says: "In order to amend the rules on job specification and assignment of lowest and highest ranks for each post of authorised official at the Ministry of the Interior, I hereby appoint the following commission ..." And we have five members listed.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The commission was being formed in order to amend the rules on job specification and assignment of ranks. According to the document, the commission had five members.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the penultimate paragraph, what is the deadline set for the proposal?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the 30th of April 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us have the next document. It is your tab 64. Exhibit 4D77. Do you have it in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Have a look at the date of the document.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We can see that the number is strictly confidential K/P-101695. The date is 2 August 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I see another date, the date when the document was received which is the 15th of August 1995.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Subject is regulations on the classification of tasks and duties in the Ministry of the Interior directed at lower organisational units?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Therefore on 15 August, they still did not have the new regulations on the classifications of tasks and duties based on which they could pursue that exercise in their units?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This document points to the fact that by mid-August, there had been no application of the regulations under classifications of tasks because it had to be in keeping with all of the documentation of the MUP that had to do with the classification of tasks and duties. This document was sent to all employees of the MUP for information.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The counsel is off mic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: A few last questions about the documents you analysed. When were the ranks finally confirmed in the Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The timing was rather slow. In the end, the ranks were regulated as late as October 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let's look at the last two documents. The first is your tab 65. Exhibit 4D361. Let us look at the date of the document. It is the 20th of October 1995. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: According to this decision, on early promotion to higher rank, it is obvious that a Mr. Borovcanin was early promoted to the rank of colonel, but his first established rank had been that of major?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The last document I wanted to look at is tab 66. It is 4D531. It is a decree number 01-197/97 of the RS president Biljana Plavsic dated the 21st of April 1997. By this decree Colonel Ljubomir Borovcanin is being promoted early to the rank of police major-general?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bajagic, I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lazarevic. Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I shan't cross-examine this witness, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I do have a few questions, Mr. President, if I may. I would need the podium.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good morning, professor. My name is John Ostojic. I represent a gentleman who is a colonel in the VRS in 1995 by the name of Ljubisa Beara. How are you?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning to you, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I have a couple of questions and just bear with me here. First, I'd like to ask you about your CV ever so briefly. I noticed that you worked in the MUP in Serbia. I just don't have the dates there in your CV, so if you could just give me those dates again that would be helpful. If you turn to your CV and I'll direct you exactly to the section I'm referring to. Under the employment it says MUP of the Republic of Serbia police academy assistant intern and assistant. What year was that?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was from September 1996, I was hired as an intern assistant at the police academy which had certain organisational functional ties with the ministry of the Internal Affairs. That is why I referred to the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The one below that sir, it says state security service of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia, what year was that where you did the training research centre, lecture?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not the state security service but the state security department. I taught there intelligence and counterintelligence at their educational centre. I was there as a lecturer.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What years?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was in 2002.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, because what I'd like to go and focus some of my questions to you on the issue of reporting and the obligations of MUP personnel to report things that they may have seen or heard. But I'd like to know first if the same reporting requirements that you discuss in your rather exhaustive report also are similar to those that are in Serbia. Are they the same or do the rules change from Serbia to the Republika Srpska, if you know, in 1995?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
