utterances.text: I never had occasion to study any rules of reporting for the Republic of Serbia. As you can see from my CV, I focused on completely different areas as a lecturer. I never analysed any documents referring to the Republic of Serbia as regards these issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Because in your report you talk and you make some comparisons to Great Britain and what their rules and obligations may be, as well as the United States of America. Are you telling me that you don't know what the reporting requirements are of MUP personnel from the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The examples of Great Britain, Germany and Croatia, I believe, were there as regards to administrative police activities, and it was specific to this report. I analysed those only so as to be able to provide a comparative view. As for reporting and informing, I never read any manuals for the MUP of Serbia because I was never operationally involved with the MUP of Serbia. I do believe, however, that for the most part, they are similar to the similar regulations of the countries and its environs in times of peace. In Serbia, there was no state of national necessity as it was the case with Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And I'll move away from that subject. Thank you. Sir, I'd like us to look at a couple of documents, but first I want to ask you, because you looked at some documents from a person by the name of Dragomir Vasic. Are you familiar or have you seen documents from Dragomir Vasic where he reports that there was no cooperation from the VRS in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know precisely. Perhaps I could look at the document and then offer a comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We'll get to the document in a second. Are you aware that Dragomir Vasic also in July of 1995 reports to his superior in the MUP that there was no assistance from the VRS? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When drafting the report, I read a plethora of documents but it doesn't necessarily mean that all are being referred to in the report itself. I stress again, if we are talking about a specific document, please let me have a look at it and then I may provide you with a comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And I will. You will get a chance to look at it and I would appreciate your comment on it, but I just wanted to know if you were familiar with it just generally speaking or if you have a recollection of it. Now, are you familiar at all or do you recall seeing a document where -- go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, probably there were some. Some were singled out in my report as well. But without the specific document at hand, I can't provide anything more precise than this, any conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I understand that. And are you aware that Dragomir Vasic also in a report in July, I think 13th, of 1995 states that the MUP was acting alone in certain operations or in a certain operation. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I would just like to be fair to the witness. This is an expert witness. He was talking about procedures. He was talking about laws and rules which were in application at the time. He didn't talk at all about any particular events. So if I don't know what kind of -- if my colleague is trying to impeach the witness's credibility with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Of course not, of course not. I am just asking him if he recalls it and my next question is to ask the Court to place P62 on the screen. But I wanted to know if he has an independent recollection of it, but if he speaks of procedures he should also know the procedures if there was a detachment from MUP and the VRS at any time, specifically in July of 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let me consult with my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Ostojic, you need to put the document and any other documents that you have to the witness and ask him directly on those documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Oh, okay. Thank you, Mr. President. Can we have P62, please, on the e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Professor, we have both or soon the English version as well but you are looking at the B/C/S version of this document that's dated the 13th of July 1995. We'll give you an opportunity to review it. Let me know when you've had that chance.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've read the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Because the next document I think follows this document but just maybe you could help me. If you see the number on the top where it says actually "number" in B/C/S, it's 282/95. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know what that means?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the year and probably the document number and the document was sent that year from an organisational unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, having read this document, to whom is Dragomir Vasic sending this report to?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the MUP of Republika Srpska to the office of the minister at Pale or also to the police forces staff in Bijeljina as well as to the public security department. There are three addressees or at least that is what is indicated here.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And I think you said "or" and it was correctly typed out but I think you meant "and" also to the police forces staff in Bijeljina, right, it's "and," not that he is sending it to one or the other, he is sending it to all three; correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. To the police forces staff in Bijeljina, to the office of the minister in Pale, and to the public security department.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I want to really focus on the second paragraph in this Exhibit P62 and there's several words maybe you could help me with. You see in the first sentence it states: "We have no cooperation or assistance from the VRS ... " Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We had no cooperation and no assistance with the VRS in doing what, sir? Well, read on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I have to object at this point. I mean, these are facts that Mr. Bajagic simply -- in my humble opinion he really cannot testify about these particular events. As for the formal right, as for to whom it was sent, as to everything about the facts, he is not a factual witness and he is not aware of anything of the kind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you wish to reply, Mr. Ostojic?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No, not really.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, I appreciate that. I do support Mr. Ostojic's position with respect to this matter. This document contains a specific content which I think is the witness entitled to opine about concerning the appropriate subject matter for the reporting requirements which he has identified in this case, and I support Mr. Ostojic in that application.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Our decision is as follows: Assuming all -- or assuming that the witness is in a position to answer this question, he must limit himself to the generics, you answer within a generic way without going into specifics for the time being, unless you are asked for them.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure I fully understand but I'll try my best here, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's see whether he is in a position to answer your question to start with.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the first reading of this document, I can see that Mr. Dragomir Vasic has noticed some problems, but I wouldn't be able to engage in any further analysis because in my expert report I did not deal with any facts or relationships on the ground. My main concern was the legal framework, that was the subject of my analysis. However, I can say based on logic that there were problems, but I wouldn't be able to tell you what problems those were.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, Mr. Vasic goes on and says the problems he expects he is going to have, but we won't ask you that fact. Let's keep it a little generic. When Dragomir Vasic creates these reports and those that you reviewed, they are required to be honest and factual, are they not?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I don't know how this witness can answer this thing. I mean, whether Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He could answer it based on his experience.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Generically, I mean generally speaking do you --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Otherwise --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He could have information which in his mind could cast doubts on the reliability of this document and the author of the -- and its author. But it's up to you to tell us whether you have sufficient information to be able to answer Mr. Ostojic's question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know anything about Dragomir Vasic, save for what I could read about what he was at a given moment in the public security centre. I don't know anything else to be able to tell you whether he was honest or dishonest, sincere or not sincere. I don't know how you put it. I don't know anything about that. I only know and that is what I said in my report when I spoke about the modalities of informing and reporting that somebody who was in charge of the centre, the chief of that centre was duty-bound to inform the top echelons at the ministry about any possible events or occurrences and that's all. I don't know whether this is a satisfactory answer, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It is what it is. Let me ask you this, sir, if he reports or -- strike that. You spent a lot of time in your report and your testimony these couple of days talking about how there was this special unit that was moved over under the auspices purportedly of the VRS. Did you find anywhere in any of the documents, other than the one you are looking at, that the MUP was working alone? Did you find those words by anybody that they made that declaration, as opposed to with the VRS? But to be fair to you, I invite you to look at that document and again that second paragraph and it's in the second to the last line of that paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I see that the witness may have some difficulties in reading the documents. Could we zoom in the B/C/S. Okay. All right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] According to Mr. Dragomir Vasic's words, in the sentence that the MUP is independent in the section, the answer would be yes. But that's the only thing I can see in this dispatch.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, based on your experience and work in this case, what does it mean when MUP works alone? Is that going back to the structures that you've highlighted when they are not directed to go back or not directed to attach themselves as a combat group with the VRS?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were several situations so far when we have stated that the units of the Ministry of the Interior were parts of the Armed Forces. That certain units or parts of these units in particular situations acted in concert with the Army of Republika Srpska. According to the principle of resubordination and the other part of those units could act pursuant to the orders of the Supreme Command which were conveyed via the Minister of the Interior as a commander of the staff of the Armed Forces of the ministry, which means that not all the units acted as parts of the army. There were some parts of the units or some units that were engaged along the lines of command from the top of the ministry to the public security stations depending on the situations on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Professor, what you are telling me is theoretical and I understand that and it's based upon the laws and the regulations that you've highlighted for us these last few days, but I'm talking about factually speaking looking at this document, if we accept it as being true that here is a guy Dragomir Vasic reporting to the MUP, and I can tell you, although you probably know this, there was no response from the minister of interior denying that MUP should be working alone or questioning whether or not MUP is working alone, but take that as a given for my hypothetical, what does it mean when he says MUP is working alone?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It's a call for speculation. Obvious one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can you answer this question or not? Because if you can only speculate, then we don't need it, we don't need your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot provide any further explanations. I've already said everything I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay, Professor. Let me try with this Exhibit, P886. If we could have both the English and the B/C/S version up. As it's being brought up I'll just give you a little background on it. It's a letter or a report from Dragomir Vasic dated the 13th of July 1995. I'm going to ask to you see what the serial number is on top or the number we refer to, because the one we just looked at was 282/95, which was Exhibit P62, this is P886, and just give us that number, if you could see it.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, throughout 1995. But the last digit in the number is 3, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Looks like --

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Or I could assume that it could also be 8. It could be either 3 or 8. I can't see the first one fully, it's not clear. It's not legible.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And in English also they were not sure so they put a question mark 83/95, and that's fair. I just wanted to know if you could see it. But it would seem that this report follows the prior one in any event because it talks about the same thing and I'd like you to read it but to direct your attention again to the first paragraph where it talks about what the army was doing and they were continuing towards Zepa and then it goes on to say "... and leaving all other work to the MUP as follows." We'll get into the things below that but I wanted you to focus on that sentence there.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see the bottom part of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I think he is asking to see the bottom part. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. It's fine, I've seen the document, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I want to focus on paragraph number 2 of this document for a moment, where Dragomir Vasic after saying everything is being left -- all the work is being left for MUP, he talks about "... killing of about 8.000 Muslim soldiers whom we blocked in the woods near Konjevic Polje. Fighting is going on. This job is being done solely by MUP units." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see this as item 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, generically speaking, I guess, if a MUP person such as Dragomir Vasic reports to his superior, and I know you went through this analysis of I think it was horizontal, vertical and diagonal reporting, and we will get to that in a little bit, but when he makes this report, is he reporting it in all three-ways, horizontally, vertically, and diagonally?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I cannot put myself in the head of Mr. Dragomir Vasic. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking you to do that because we are talking generic now. Is he required to report it in those three manners, vertically, horizontally, and diagonally? I mean we could also look at the top of that page and see whom he really sends this report to, can we not, and then deduce from that that indeed he does do it all three ways? But let's talk generically, and you tell me, sir, do you think that he is required to send it in those three manners?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not what is requested from him. He is duty-bound to abide by the instruction on reporting within the Ministry of the Interior. This is his duty. There should be no particular special requests or orders upon him to do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And I --

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And this is just one type or kind of reporting.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, I want to not backtrack, but now put it maybe in more focus. If we could look at 4D339, please. And as it's being brought up, I'll just let you know that this is also a report from Dragomir Vasic but from the day before. And you are welcome to read the whole report, sir, if you wish, but really I want to focus on the three subparagraphs in the second half of this report which bear the numbers 1, 2, and 3. Do you see that? Again, this is one day before this discussion we had about where Dragomir Vasic says no cooperation, no assistance on the 13th, they are working alone. I want to look at those three paragraphs and really highlight the fact that in paragraphs 1 and 3 he mentions actions that were undertaken that were in cooperation with the VRS, but on number 2 he clearly doesn't state that; correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I've read all the three items. If you are referring to the lower part of the dispatch under 1, 2 and 3. Under 2 it says that one -- and it is only natural, my only comment can be general. These are some special security tasks dealing with providing security for roads. This is not an exclusively combat task. And number 2 speaks about the engagement of certain units of the Ministry of the Interior in cooperation of the units of the VRS. This is what I see. And this is something that Mr. Dragomir Vasic reports about and sends a report to others. These are general facts. I can see that there is cooperation. I can see that one part of the unit is independent and that its other part is in cooperation with the army. This is all I can say. None of these facts, facts about the traffic, roads, some of these settlements, none of it, this is too familiar to me and there's nothing in particular, no particular conclusion I can draw upon reading this.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let me just then at the very least try to correct the record, because on page 54, lines 25 and then proceeding on page 55, lines 1 and 2, they recorded you as saying that paragraph number 2 indicates that there was cooperation with respect to this operation with the VRS, but plainly, sir, that's not accurate and I'm not suggesting that you said it wrong. I'm just suggesting perhaps it was just recorded wrong. With respect to the ambushes in number 2, there is no language whatsoever that indicates there was any cooperation with the VRS; correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is obvious it transpires from item 2, however.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I just wanted to correct the record because I think they misheard you, that's all, and so I'm not challenging you on it and I think it's pretty obvious myself.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well then.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thanks. I read your report and I really had a little trouble with a couple of paragraphs and I want to direct your attention if I may to paragraph 256 which is on page 65 of your report. And I think it may be, sir, that it was translated, with all due respect, somewhat awkwardly but I don't know what your point was in the next ten paragraphs. It says, and I'll read it: "Information in the police understands in general sense a planned set of the procedures by which is gathered, processed (analysis, classification, checking, and uniting) the information relating to: Security situation, phenomenon, and events, the work and results of the police station work, and the situation in the police station." I read this, honestly, 20 times. I don't understand what you are trying to say here. And I apologise for having to ask you.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are we talking about paragraph 256?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This means that informing implies a group of procedure intended to collect, process, safeguard, use and provide security information and data which relate to what, security situation, events, occurrences, the work of the police stations and situation in the police station. I don't know what is not clear. In parentheses --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: This is too fast for the interpreter and we apologise.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The processing of any kind of information implies --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Excuse me. The translators just give us an indication you may be speaking too fast. I'm not going to cut you off and just before you answer if I can just make a preliminary -- I'm not, sir, challenging you on this. I just wanted to understand it and honestly in English it's a little difficult to understand the way it's written so I'm just trying to have you help me fully understand it. But if you can please just speak a little slower, that may help all of us to understand it.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well, I'll try to be as clear as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think we are going to waste much time. I think that the problem with paragraph 256, the translation into English; otherwise I think if you read it a second time, it's sufficient to understand what it means.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay, I'll move on, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Excuse me, excuse me. The paragraph 256 as it appears in the monitor is different from what I have as a final or translation. I think this is an unofficial translation, and this is different from what I have in hard copies. Probably this is older version.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Honourable Judge Kwon, I'll take a look at it that. I wanted clarification on this one paragraph because it begins a process of other things, but I -- we'll look at that again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PROST
utterances.text: And, Mr. Ostojic, if you look at the one that's in e-court, it reads differently from what you read out as well, so I think it may be a translation issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Fair enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Maybe I can just explain, one Mr. Bajagic filed his report in B/C/S, it was unofficially translated by the Defence in order to comply to Trial Chamber's order regarding deadlines for filing the reports. After that the CLSS provided with their official translation which is in the EDS system.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's very fair. I apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I just wanted to understand it because I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, if we look at paragraph 260 of your report on that same page, and I am working with the apparently non-updated version, but it doesn't matter. I'm not going to pick on the language. You say within information reporting has a special place. Pretty much the same. Why and how does it have a special place?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Reporting is one of the actions within the system of informing. It implies informing starting with the bottom to the top and as a rule reports are sent about a concrete task, the implementation of a concrete task that had been given to members of the police, either uniformed police, crime prevention police and so on and so forth. Or, if an order has been issued to the members of the police to carry out a task immediately upon the completion of the task, they have to report about the status of the task, whether it has been fully completed, partly completed, so this is an activity by way of which lower levels report to the higher levels within the hierarchy of command.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, we -- it's like the reports we saw from Dragomir Vasic reporting to the minister; correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that would be one of the forms of reporting.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, these reports, they are required to be clear and precise; correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And also they are required to be a fair and adequate reflection of what is transpiring, is it not?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In general terms the answer would be yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, when I look at your paragraph 262, you also talk about elements from the environment in the second line, I hope, at least in my copy. I just wanted you to explain it to me because I didn't fully understand it.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It has to do with a head of a certain organisational unit in the ministry represents that unit before the higher organisational levels, as well as in communication with the organisations at the same level and below. He represents his organisational unit before the other organisational levels within the police system. It can be, as I said, internally, meaning inside the ministry, and externally if there is a possibility for the head of a certain level organisation of the ministry for him to meet representatives of some other institutions. On such occasions, he is also there to speak on behalf of his organisational unit. I tried to make this as clear as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, generally speaking, what types of information are required or mandated to be put in such reports that you are referring to, both the external and internal, and I don't know that it really matters, but really during the state of war or imminent threat of war? What type of information are they required to report?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Internal representation is quite different from external representation especially when we are talking about the MUP. Internally it can include anything that is of importance for the conducting of tasks and duties of the police. External representation doesn't deal with such issues. External representation is representing a certain part of the ministry when communicating with some other ministries or bodies during meetings. Therefore the facts discussed at such meetings are not the same as would be during an internal representation event. This would be a global information with far less details.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's talk about like if there was an ambush or a legitimate combat engagement that was going on in July of 1995. What would the reporting requirements be in the MUP now, just in the MUP, as to what kind of information should be contained within that report to their superiors?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Important information needed to be included in order to report to a higher level of management within the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. And now --

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Anything that would be necessary for efficient functioning in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Certainly one of the things they would possibly report - I'll let you answer it - is if there were any casualties or wounded of MUP personnel; correct?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And I agree of course it would be. And also they would highlight where certain MUP units were acting alone or acting in conjunction with some other groups, would it not? That would be significant to report to your superior?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I presume so.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: You are the expert though, so you help me with that. They would also report, would they not, if they were involved in any operations such as ambushes or capturing or killing the enemy combatants, would they not?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, maybe I'm a bit late with my objection but I believe that this asks for some incomplete hypothetical speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Ostojic, do you wish to move on?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Fair enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just describe for me, if you will, what you meant on paragraph 256 when you talked about the information representation relating to phenomenon and events, if we could just scroll down so I could see it because I'm not sure if it's translated that way again, the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What do you mean by that, what events and what phenomenon?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I hereby say security situation, events, and phenomenon. Well, that includes anything that takes place in a given territory that is of importance for the functioning of the MUP units as one of the security actors or subjects.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure if you said it right but I thought I heard it in B/C/S and it's recorded as being any, but you are saying everything, right, as opposed to anything? Although it may be a slight difference. They are supposed to report on everything, are they not, Professor?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise, this question is not clear. Who is Mr. Ostojic referring it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It's pretty obvious I think if the Professor in his report sets forth that there are certain requirements that go in three different manners both vertically and horizontally, so whoever is preparing the report such as Dragomir Vasic, but we don't want to include him right now in this, but any of the people who are either the -- in the CJP or PJP or SJP, whatever those centres are, are they required to report and what are they required to put in their report, that's all I'm trying to get from you. I think it's in your report but I just wanted to know in a war situation what types of things are they really supposed to report?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I stated in paragraph 256, that these are occurrences and events. I've primarily had those in mind which are important for the security in the territory and anything else that can be important for the work and functioning of the Ministry of the Interior. In that regard, I wrote the security information, what does it mean to inform? That means that the security situation can be reported as improving or deteriorating. Then there are developments and events that the number of traffic accidents increased and so on and so forth. This information and representation, generally speaking, refers to information being circulated through the police bodies not only at times of war but also at peacetime and during imminent threat of war. As for such particular information should include that exact period, I can't say. I can only speak hypothetically. It is impossible for me to answer that because I have no such specific experience with those modes of reporting.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much. Professor, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I have no questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am Natasha Fauveau-Ivanovic. I represent General Miletic. I wish to ask you a few questions which are theoretical. You spoke on the 6th of October, on first day of your testimony on the task of the police, in particular the task which the police accomplish when there is an threat of imminent war and you also spoke a moment or two ago of those tasks in particular, the traffic regulation, special regulation of traffic. I would like you to look at the document 5D1318. We do not have an official translation of this document, but we have a draft translation which I have here, and I have a hard copy for the member of the Chamber. So this document is an order from the Ministry of the Interior which concerns stopping the traffic on the Sokolac on the 26 June 1995 and what I would like you to do is to read this document and also tell us if this order -- the task given by the police in this order fits in the normal task of the police in the situation which is described here, that is to say, in a situation where you have sabotage groups and terrorist groups which have come into the territory.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is one of the tasks of the police. The police has authority to implement such tasks, special security circumstances. We can see what is being requested from the order and we see that it doesn't entail any combat but regulating the traffic, setting up a checkpoint and controlling the traffic on certain roads. These are special security circumstances because of the terrorist groups. But it is a non-combat administrative activity on the part of the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Activities which or so it means stopping the traffic on that particular road, this is what can be read in the first sentence of the document?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so. To stop the traffic on a particular road. According to the law on the application of the Law on Internal Affairs from 1994, the authorities of the police in the state of imminent threat of war or in the state of war. One of the authorities described is this one.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Ms. Fauveau needs to wait for the English translation to finish, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I need to apologise to Madam Fauveau. I really hate to interrupt someone cross-examining, but we still haven't received the list of documents which are to be used in the cross-examination of the Defence or the translation of these documents. Maybe she can take care of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We have received it. So I don't know what to tell you, Mr. Lazarevic. But to my knowledge it has been circulated. The other thing is the interpreters drew our attention to tell you that you need to wait until the English translation is finished before you proceed with your question, please, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: I would like now to show you document 51319 for which there is an official translation. Sir, I don't want to ask anything about the contents of the document but the only thing I'm interested in is to know whether this document which it's a document which in the province of the state security, I think, is this document based on information obtained by the intelligence services? Is this type of information coming, rather, from intelligence sources?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That means if you are in a position to tell us, please. If you are not, don't speculate.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is quite clear from the very same abbreviation, the RDB which is the state security department, that this information arrived from that direction and is of intelligence or counterintelligence nature.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Thank you very much, this is quite sufficient for what I wish to know. Could one say indeed that the activities of the intelligence services or the principle main [indiscernible] in the sector of the state security?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: I wish to ask you a few questions concerning the engagement of police units in activities in combats. You spoke about this yesterday. I don't think you need to repeat what was already said. I wish you to see document 5D1320. We still have here an unofficial translation here, and we have a hard copy translation for the members of the Chamber. Here we have a document from the Ministry of Interior transmitting, forwarding a dispatch from the staff of the army of the Republika Srpska. You explained to us yesterday all the procedure for the engagement of police units in the combat activities. Could you simply have a look at this document, one-page document, and tell us whether this procedure was conforming to the procedure prescribed by law, by the law?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we can see that the president of the republic did order the units to be used and that it was requested that certain units be put under the 14th, but I don't know what the abbreviation stands for.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters apologise. Under the commander's request -- the speakers should not overlap and they should wait for the English translation. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, this is my fault. I interrupted you and therefore you couldn't hear. Could you please repeat the last part of your answer. Does this document show that the procedure was conforming to the procedure which the law had provided for?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the president of the republic ordered it and it was followed up according to the established procedure.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I see that it's time for the break but I only need a couple of minutes. Could I continue and finish?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I would suggest that you do that and we have the break after that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Lastly, I would like to examine the document 1321. This is still dealing with the same topic that is the engagement of police units in combat. Again I have an unofficial translation for the Chamber. While we are waiting, could you have a look at the document, perhaps we need to have a zoom.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: According to this document, the public security centre in Zvornik sent on June 21st a unit to the front where the Republika Srpska was having -- was losing soldiers and they sent a dispatch and another unit was sent from Zvornik. Do you agree that according to this document, you cannot see that there was any request coming from the army so that these units be sent to fight side by side with the army of the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see from the document that there were any written requests. It probably all took place in the field presumably. However, the police forces staff commander of the CSB in Zvornik according to some legal provisions has the right to engage certain units but he urgently needs to notify the minister and the police forces staff at headquarters. It was probably due to a certain situation in the field. I do know what the law states as to what the public security centre commander of the police forces staff can do, he can do it but he needs to urgently report to the ministry and headquarters. This is all I can tell you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Krgovic or Mr. Josse, do you have any questions for this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: We don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Mr. Sarapa?

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Briefly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You have some questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. We'll have your questions immediately after the break, and then -- do you wish to state something, Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, not really, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. How long do you think you will be cross-examining this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, I'll confer with Mr. McCloskey, but I anticipate about half an hour to 40 minutes. I don't know if we can make it but I'll do my best, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I can release the witness who is waiting here since the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is why I have asked the question. As it is, shall we send the witness. For the rest of this week you've got this next witness and another one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And another one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And another one. All right. Can you just make me a rough calculation, okay, I will ask my staff to do it. How long they will be testifying. Okay. We'll have a 25-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Sarapa. For the record, we have now the company of Mr. Bourgon. Yes, Mr. Sarapa.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm Djorde Sarapa and I represent Vinko Pandurevic. Dr. Bajagic, I have just one question for you. Members of the security and intelligence organs and services of the Army of Republika Srpska had legal authorities in acting within their purview which were adequate to the authorities of members of the MUP of Republika Srpska within the department of state security. Please tell us what authorities were those when it comes to the members of the MUP of Republika Srpska within the state security department?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I start?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know whether the authorities were the same because I never analysed that matter. And as far as the state security department is concerned, that element of the Ministry of the Interior had a task to collect information, i.e., intelligence and counterintelligence that concerned the security of Republika Srpska and the implementation of its interest. This is in very general terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: And in operative sense, would you please be more precise?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can try. Collecting intelligence and counterintelligence by all methods known to all intelligence and counterintelligence services in the world. I can give you their list.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Collection of intelligence from human sources or human intelligence as it is theoretically known, collection of intelligence from open sources, or open search intelligence. Collection of intelligence by technical methods in a narrow and broader sense, method of collaboration or cooperation with informants, and all the other scientific methods that are normally used in the processing of intelligence and counterintelligence. In general terms, those are methods of intelligence services and security department applied all these matters when it came to collecting intelligence within its purview.

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you Mr. President. Good afternoon to you, good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to my colleagues and good afternoon to you, Dr. Bajagic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: My name is Kweku Vanderpuye on behalf of the Prosecution. I'm going to put some questions to you in relation to your direct examination as well as your cross-examination by some of my colleagues in the Defence. If there's anything I ask you that is not clear, please let me know. I'll do my best to try and clarify things so that we can understand each other a little bit better. I hope to be able to finish with you so let's get right to it. You said, I believe in your direct examination that you were an operative in the national security service which then became the public security state security service, is that right, and that was in 1992 that you began there?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And during the course of the war, is that where you were -- well, tell us where you were and what you did.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I worked as an operative which means I was a professional in the service which was the national security service first and then became the skate security service. In more concrete terms, if you are asking me for the region, I was posted in Sarajevo in Ilidza and I was dealing with collection of intelligence and counterintelligence as any operative will do, and this was within the purview of the state security department and this purview had legal foundations. It was regulated by law.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And during the period of that period of time, you tell us who was the Minister of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to the entire period that I spent working in the department?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: If I could ask you that and then I will be more specific.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll try and remember. There were some shakeups in the organisation. The first minister I believe was Mico Stanisic at the very beginning in 1992 and I would not be able to follow the right sequence. I know that at one point it was Zivko Rakic. I know that at some other point it was another gentleman whom I can't remember. I can't remember his name. I believe that his family name was Adzic. I don't know when he was in office and I also know that about the time when I was leaving the state security sector and the Ministry of the Interior, Dragan Kijac was about to be appointed or just took up the position and this is all I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you remember if a Zivko Rakic was the Minister of the Interior in 1995 at any point?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't remember but since we have analysed certain documents, I believe that he is referred to as the Minister of the Interior, Republika Srpska in office in 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And in relation to that, do you recognise the name of Tomislav Kovac?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you know what his position was in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that Tomislav Kovac was deputy minister of the interior of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Now, you know that during the course of the war, 1995, there was a front in Sarajevo, around Sarajevo that was within the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps; right?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well ...

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you came into that information I take it, during the course of your employment in the state security service; right?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. I was in the territory of Sarajevo so not just me but everybody else knew that Sarajevo was within the zone of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And with respect to your knowledge of how the state security service operated, was it the case that the state security service shared information with other organs, such as the public security service, public security sectors, police directorate, and so on and so forth?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sure of that but I personally did not have the right to share any information. The information was sent to my supervisors and further up to the top of the state security. I never participated in any exchange of information. I had to act in keeping with the rules of the service. But I'm sure that there was cooperation. It is only natural that information was exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Is the nature of the information that is exchanged information that is gathered on the ground, for example, through operatives with the state security?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only that. This included information gathered through operatives, but this is not the only way intelligence was collected. There are other ways as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, in particular I'm interested in knowing how the intelligence was shared and with whom it was shared from the state security services. So if you could, just briefly tell us with what agencies, what organs in information was shared?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As an operative, I could send the intelligence that I collected to my supervisors. As for them, who they shared the intelligence with according to the rules of service or how the exchange took place with the state security services from the top to the public security, I really don't know how it went, whether it was daily, weekly monthly. I personally was not in a position to participate in the exchange of information of intelligence at the level at which I operated.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, it is the case that you've given lectures in respect of intelligence practices, no?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You published in that area, isn't that true? Think you said you have over 50 publications?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. Precisely so, yes. Particularly dealing with the process of collection of intelligence. Not every work of mine deals with that, but the main body of my work is concerned with that particular issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can give you more specific details about the entire process of collecting intelligence.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: No, I'm not interested in the specific details of how -- well, I am but I don't think I have time to get into that. But what I'd like to know specifically is in the context of your experience and your expertise in the area of intelligence work, what agencies corresponded with the state security services in terms of sharing information?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Surely it would be the public security department through the office of the minister and the minister himself. And surely it would be through the department of state security that other agencies which were provided for by the law to deal with the protection of security in Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. So in the context of security, it is the case that the state security service or sector would provide information to the public security department, right, and the public security department would forward that information within its own chain? That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would sooner say that within the office of the minister, the head of the department of state security would brief the Minister of the Interior and the chief of the public security department, and whether things were done in a similar way at lower levels both of the RDB and the security services centres following some specific set of instructions, I really wouldn't be able to tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Within say, for example, the CJB in Zvornik, now, is there -- sorry, the CSB. I'm sorry. Can you tell us what information it is -- well, could that particular service share information with the public security sector of that division?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that you have worded your question well, but I'm still getting the drift. If you are referring to Zvornik, you are talking about the relationship between the security services centre and the public security centre. I'm not sure that I got the meaning right. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What I'm talking about is I'm talking about the public security centre in Zvornik. That's the CJB. Did they receive information from the intelligence -- did they receive information from state security?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose so because the state security informs public security and then this goes to the CJB in Zvornik. That was the line that communication went down on, so I suppose the answer would be yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Can you tell us who was the head of state security in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember the name. I wouldn't be able to tell you for most of the chiefs. I could probably remember the person in Sarajevo, but no, not for Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did state security have a parallel or similar chain down from the regional to the municipal and to the local, as you've indicated public security did?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We can say that it is similar, but it is still very specific because every intelligence and counterintelligence service is particularly engaged in protecting its information system and channels. I'm sure that the manners of internal exchange of information was different in the state security. I believe that they followed much stricter rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Are you saying you don't actually know whether or not the state security services were organised on a regional and municipal level, or are you saying that you just don't know who in particular was working say, for example, in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, I thought you asked me about informing so I would like to confirm that the state security service was organised at the regional and territorial levels in state security centres and departments thereof. For example, the headquarters of the state security is one thing. The centre of the state security centre in Sarajevo is one step below according to the territorial system of organisation. And there would also be a department or several departments within the regional centre. But the departments did not consign with municipalities. For example one department could comprise two municipalities or just one.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you know the name Sinisa Glogovac?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Tell us who he is.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a member of the state security department just like me from 1992 to 1992 [as interpreted] and he worked for the state security services of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina even before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what is reflected in the record page 77, line 9 is that he worked from 92 to 92, but I'm sure that can't be right. So I wonder if you could just clarify that?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It should be 1995, the second year should be 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And in 1995, do you know where he was working?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly where he was working in 1995, in which department or centre, which of these he was affiliated with.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the name Vitomir Tomic?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Now, you indicated that you were assigned to work in Sarajevo and that's throughout your tenure with state security; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, because I also resided in Sarajevo. To be more precise, I resided in the municipality of Ilidza.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'd like to show you a document if I could in e-court. 65 ter 3792. Just to let you know, I guess while it's being loaded in e-court, this is a document that was written by Ljubisa Borovcanin and it's dated 30 June 1995. I think it will be up in just a minute. Okay. And you can see in this document it's dated the 30th of June 1995. The number of it is 114/95 and it's directed to the Minister of the Interior for information. It's also directed to the head of RJB. It's directed to the police forces headquarters from Pale. It's directed to the police force headquarters chief of Bijeljina MUP, and the police forces headquarters of Vogosca. Now, in this document you can see the first paragraph he talks about having informed these organs or individuals about a situation in the field in the zone of responsibility kept by five of our PJP companies and one company comprised of MUP members. What he talks about if you look further down the document, is he lists several units. He says, "We emphasize that the unit came to the field in the following order: One Trebinje PJP company, one MUP company in the headquarters, one Bijeljina CJB PJP company, one Srbinje PJP company, one Banja Luka PJP company. Just above his signature he talks about the current situation in the field, the level of moral, the PJP members are firmly holding the achieved positions. In the context of this document, can you tell us who it is -- well, who is in charge of these PJP companies?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to what I can see in the heading, could we go back to the top of the document. We have the units and on the top we have the police forces staff. This in turn means that these units were put under that particular staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Just above his signature he talks about how they are holding their achieved positions. Is that suggesting that these units are engaged in combat?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we are talking about positions occupied, that's probably what they had in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And that being the case, it would make sense that those units would be subordinated to the VRS corps in that area. Does that make sense?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could make sense but there are two situations in which MUP units can be engaged in a time of war. They can act independently, and they can act as a part of the VRS based on the principle of resubordination. I see nothing here that would make me able to conclude which of these two actually took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Well, under Article 14 of the law on implementation of the Law of Internal Affairs, if they were engaged in combat they would be under the immediate command of Mr. Borovcanin; right?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If engaged in combat and if it was indeed the units mentioned here.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And --

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be my general conclusion based on the document. If they participated in combat, it is known that they were subordinated to the above-mentioned police reserves force. However, from the document, you can't see whether these units were resubordinated to the VRS or whether they acted independently. I truly can't argue either way based on the information I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Well, let me show you another document, if I could. Thank you, that's 3794. This, as you can see, is another report, and it is authored by Mr. Borovcanin. Was directed to the Ministry of the Interior, deputy minister in Bijeljina, Pale police staff directed to the commander, Vogosca police force staff and it says Janja special police brigade, it's dated 1st of July 1995. In this document you can see that it says refers to activities commenced the previous day which were continued at the Trnovo battle field on 30th of July 1995 and he talks about a combat group which included 5th Special Police Detachment. He talks about two platoons from the Kajman detachment, Plavi, and Skorpija, Serbian MUP attacked the facility in Lucevik. He continues on it and says in the middle of this document, the problem of respecting the agreement with the RSK Sarajevo-Romanija Corps over joint actions in overtaking lines is still present, and then in the end of the document he talks about the situation with respect to the special police brigade forces and he says they are exhausted and proposes withdrawal of some of them to the home base. Now, in this respect can you tell us who would have been in command of the Serbian MUP?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Let me back up then. In the context of this particular document, is it apparent to you who is in charge of these units, who commands these units?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can tell, these units acted in concert and it is stipulated which units took part in individual operations. However, I can't see who was in direct command of those units. This is one type of informing in which it is explained what took place during the course of a single day in a given area, but it doesn't necessarily mean that all the units referred to were commanded by a single person. The document is not clear in that regard.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. But from the document, it is certainly a possibility that the person that is making the report is in charge of these units? It's possible?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I believe it's a call for speculation. I believe the witness already said it's not clear from the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The question is specific as to the content and the nature of the communication. So I think that he is perfectly within his expertise to opine on the possibility, given the nature of the document, the content of the document, as to whether or not the author of the document is possibly in charge of these units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We think the witness can answer the question. As far as he knows obviously. But the question being asked is based on his knowledge whether there is this possibility or not. It's not speculation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wouldn't want to speculate. As I said, the document is unclear in that regard.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, in terms of the content of the document, it is consistent with a commanding officer, the nature of that information is consistent with the type of information that would be included in a document that is -- a report that is made by a commanding officer, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may be, but reports are not drafted solely by commanders and commanding officers. Reports are drafted also by services. If you have in mind all of the different types of informing that can be in place. This is a dispatch. Or an information sheet of sorts. I don't know what to call it exactly. Yes, it could be done by the commander, but also by others.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Well, it would be consistent that a commander would have a duty to report what the situation concerning the conduct in a battle field would be, right, to his superiors?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It would be consistent for a commander to report to his superiors what his expectations are with respect to the mission that he has been assigned to carry out and when he expected it would be completed; right?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, it can contain all those elements, but it is difficult to give an assessment of when a given task is to be concluded in such war circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, in the interest of time, I guess I will leave that be and I'm move on, as we've only got about five minutes left. Let me just ask you before I leave this area, how is it that we have Serbian MUP that are included among these units, if you can tell, based upon this report?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say. I read it but I can't say how and in what way it took place. These are specific facts that I would need. I can't say where that came from.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, I'm not asking about that specifically. You know, and you've commented in your expertise upon the role and the duties of the deputy commander of the special police brigade, in this case it was Mr. Borovcanin, and you know the mechanisms by which he may exercise supervision over MUP units that are in his charge, in his chain of command. So I'm asking you in a general, in a more general sense, how is it that, and when I say Serbian MUP, I mean MUP from the former -- from the FRY, how is it that they are assigned or they appear in this document in relation to the activities carried out by other members of the MUP in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I answered already that I don't know. You should ask the person who made the decision for such units to be in the field. I have no ability to answer in any other way.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. So you are not familiar with at least mechanistically as a method of organisation how it is that this could occur, at least in a theoretical sense?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you have in mind the mechanisms that existed between the Republika Srpska and the Serbian MUP, then I truly don't know what sort of mechanisms there were. I was just a simply operative at the time. These things had to be decided on by the top echelon, by the highest ranks.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Could I look at 65 ter 57, please. Sorry, in relation to my last question, you indicated that these -- the mechanism by which these Serbian MUP might find themselves in the circumstances indicated if Mr. Borovcanin's report, you said that that had to be -- that's a matter that had to be decided by the top echelon by the highest ranks, is that right, of government, I take it?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And by government, that could mean the civilian government, it could mean the army; right?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean the top level at which such a decision can be made or such ways of cooperation instituted.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That could be done through the Main Staff of the army; right? I should say the VRS so the record is clear.

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I truly don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... presidency?

utterances.speaker: MLADEN BAJAGIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I truly don't know what organ that would be. The top of the state, we know what that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, we are going until 2.00, right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: We're not. Is it possible that I could continue for a -- or should we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There is a sitting.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How much longer do you have?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I have about 15 minutes or so. I don't think I can make it shorter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I am afraid, Professor, we haven't finished. Don't blame anyone in particular. We have to continue tomorrow morning. Now, I wouldn't like to stay another 15 minutes because that would compromise things for the next Trial Chamber, will make things difficult. So let's adjourn now until tomorrow morning at 9.00. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 1.46 p.m., to be reconvened on Thursday, the 9th day of October 2008, at 9.00 a.m.
